item.title: Configure Controller Credentials
item.description:
Goal

Configure credentials to allow OCM Controllers to access OCM components stored in private OCI registries.

You will end up with

  • A Kubernetes secret containing registry credentials
  • OCM Controller resources configured to use these credentials
  • Verified access to private OCM repositories

Estimated time: ~5 minutes

item.title: Configure Custom RBAC
item.description: The OCM Kubernetes Controller Toolkit ships with the minimum RBAC permissions needed to manage its own custom resources (Repository, Component, Resource, Deployer, NamespacedDeployer). It does not include permissions for the objects your deployers create, such as kro ResourceGraphDefinitions. You grant those yourself, and who needs which verbs depends on the deployer kind:

item.title: Discover Component Graphs
item.description:
Goal

Use a Discovery resource to resolve the transitive component graph of a Component, filter it with selectors, and publish either the filtered raw descriptors or projected free-form records into the Discovery status.

item.title: Deploy with Chained kro RGDs
item.description: You have an application to run on Kubernetes. You want to ship it the same way every time: one versioned package that carries the container image and the instructions to run it. When you move that package from a development registry to production, or into an air-gapped cluster, the image references must follow automatically. You should never hand-edit a manifest to fix a registry path.

item.title: Deploy a Helm Chart with kro and GitOps
item.description:
What You’ll Learn

Your application already ships as a Helm chart, and you want its delivery to be just as repeatable: one versioned OCM component that carries the chart, its container image, and the instructions to deploy it. Promote that component from a staging registry to production, or hand it to an air-gapped cluster, and the image references should update themselves. Patching a values file to correct a registry path is exactly what this avoids.

item.title: Deploy a Helm Chart with Crossplane and GitOps
item.description:
What You’ll Learn

Your application ships as a Helm chart, and you want its delivery to be repeatable: one versioned OCM component that carries the chart, its container image, and the instructions to deploy it, with image references that localize themselves as the component moves between registries. This tutorial builds that deployment on Crossplane, using a CompositeResourceDefinition (XRD) plus a Composition to reconcile the deployment graph. The XRD registers the Bootstrap schema, and the Composition creates the OCM and GitOps deployer objects (Flux or Argo CD) directly. We will use Podinfo as the example application.

item.title: Deploy Kubernetes Manifests with the OCM Deployer
item.description: This guide shows how to deploy raw Kubernetes manifests from an OCM component version using the OCM Controllers’ built-in NamespacedDeployer. This approach requires only the OCM Controllers—no kro or Flux needed.

item.title: Deploy Crossplane Packages (xpkg) with OCM
item.description: In this tutorial, you package a Crossplane Configuration and the Function it depends on in an OCM component version, transfer them to the registry your cluster pulls from, and let the OCM Controllers and kro install them into Crossplane, pinned by digest.

item.title: Verify Component Signatures on Deployment
item.description:
Goal

Configure the OCM Kubernetes controller to automatically verify component version signatures before reconciling resources.

You’ll end up with

  • A Secret holding an OCM configuration that requests signature verification
  • A Component resource that reconciles only if the signature verifies

Estimated time: ~5 minutes
